analysis: Reviewed the two base_text excerpts (lines 26797-28169) of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json. These are public synthetic golden vectors: gemma-4 chat_completions cases (multi-tool call, json_object, json_schema) containing request_body, provider_body, template_input, plan (prompt_contract_id, block_boundaries, chain hashes) and token_ids. They contain no secrets, keys, tokens or real user data. The PR patch (partially visible, truncated) edits other regions: adds additional_context.enable_thinking=false to a template_input, and changes prompt_token_count, block_boundaries and chain hashes. The base excerpts lie outside the listed changed base ranges, so they are unchanged context; the only diff evidence is the truncated patch hunk. This is a test-fixture change with no code path, authorization, attestation, encryption or key-handling impact. Relevant threat context is T-041 (prefix-cache chain hashes and cross-tenant sharing), but fixture updates alone do not weaken any control. One integration question: the new additional_context field and the changed prompt_contract_id/token counts must correspond to a matching provider/coordinator implementation change (not supplied here), so that cache block-boundary hashing stays consistent and doesn't produce cross-contract prefix-cache reuse. This is unverified and not evidence of a regression. I could not examine the head side in full because the patch is truncated.
